# EnterpriseGlue v0.29.3 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.29.2`.

## Highlights

- **installation:** Restore compiled database upgrades, macOS shutdown, and security-qualified runtime installation with the declared Node 24 major.

## User and administrator impact

- Existing databases can run historical entity-based migrations from a compiled backend.
- Developers can stop their local Compose stack with no extra arguments on stock macOS Bash.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Build or install the corrected backend before upgrading an existing database; retain its data volume.

## Configuration

- Contributor setup documents environment bootstrapping, host database prerequisites, and the current CI commands.
- Oracle compiled smoke lets the application bootstrap its pristine disposable database and record the migration ledger; a test-only schema sync no longer creates a latest schema with an empty ledger.

## Database migrations

- Migration: 1700000000113-add-provisioning-credential-idempotency.
- Migration: 1700000000124-add-native-saas-tenancy.
- Historical migration bodies and the migration inventory are unchanged. Compiled migrations resolve the entities registered by the same compiled backend.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- No authentication or authorization policy changes.
- Application and frozen-bootstrap runtime layers require the patched glibc 2.44 family at 2.44-r8 or later, invalidating stale cached OS upgrade layers.
- The application runtime removes the vendor image Node/npm/Corepack family and installs Node 24.21.0-r4, with a hard Node-major assertion matching the declared Node 24 contract.

## Documentation

- CONTRIBUTING.md describes startup completion, non-destructive upgrades, isolated test database setup, and CI checks.
- The technical security dependency runbook documents runtime OS floors and Node-major verification.

## Known limitations

- Physical database portability and production image acceptance require their candidate gates.

## Rollback

- Restore the prior application; this change adds no migration or schema transition.

## Validation evidence

- Node 24.18.1: complete backend unit suite passed (3781 tests across 466 files); Node 24.10.0: frontend unit suite passed (1562 tests across 316 files).
- Workspace typecheck and warning-free lint passed with pnpm 11.0.8.
- Both compiled PostgreSQL historical upgrades passed with retained data and repeat-run idempotence; all ten backend/published adapter path selections passed.
- Eight actual shutdown argv cases passed under macOS Bash 3.2 with a recording Docker stub.
- CI contracts (166 tests), affected classifier contracts (51 tests), documentation boundary, release-note preflight, and package version guard passed.
- The initial Node 24.10.0 broad backend run had two HTTP socket/parser failures. All 94 tests in those files passed focused reproduction; the complete suite subsequently passed under Node 24.18.1.
- Final adapter discovery correction: 48 focused adapter/portability tests passed, and ten isolated compiled adapter probes discover only timestamped migrations. The earlier hosted matrix failed on the helper module constructor and requires fresh exact-head acceptance.
- Hosted d92b3709 passed the full physical five-adapter portability matrix. Its separate Oracle smoke exposed a current-schema/empty-ledger fixture; the fixture correction requires fresh hosted smoke acceptance.
- The native arm64 runtime base built with Node 24.21.0 and passed Trivy 0.72.0 under the unchanged all-severity policy with zero unignored findings; vulnerability DB updated 2026-10-08 15:33 UTC and downloaded 17:14 UTC. Full application and bootstrap acceptance remains mandatory.
- All eight published packages built, packed and passed host/toolchain tarball entrypoint and dependency-reference verification.
- Native backend, frontend and frozen-bootstrap images built and passed fresh Trivy all-severity scans with zero unignored findings; real PostgreSQL bootstrap/idempotence/receipt/drift checks passed with the updated bootstrap image.
- The exact native application image ran Node 24.21.0, became ready against a pristine owned PostgreSQL database, and became ready after restart against the retained database.
